content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket carefully.

The employee E029 (Jesus Cooke) requests write access to Source Code.

There are two notes in shared memory:
- Note 1 says: role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommendation write. Comment says full-time employee allowed up to write.
- Note 2 says: role Payroll Specialist, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Comment says Security DB shows E029 is a contractor with basic security training; the note listing full_time is outdated/incorrect. Contractors get read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training => max read. Requested write is above max, so grant read.

So there's a conflict. Note 2 says the memory in note 1 is outdated/incorrect. Note 2 appears to be from the Security agent (since it references Security DB). Note 1 may be from HR agent.

As the Approver, I need to make the final decision based on the information available. The more recent/corrected information says the employee is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors with basic training max = read. Requested write is above max, so grant read.

The policy: contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

So for a contractor with basic training, max is read. Grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.
